Our 4 th Integrated Report provides a comprehensive overview of our strategy, performance, governance and value creation. It underscores our dedication to responsible and sustainable business practices that drive positive outcomes for the economy, the environment, and the communities we serve, creating value for all our stakeholders.

This report provides an overview of our performance and articulates how our strategy is structured to create value for our stakeholders over the short, medium and long term.

Certain statements in this Report regarding our business operations may constitute forward-looking statements. These include all statements other than statements of historical facts, including those regarding the financial position, business strategy, management plans and objectives for future operations. Forward-looking statements can be identified by words such as ‘believes’, ‘estimates’, ‘anticipates’, ‘expects’, ‘may’, ‘will’, ‘plans’, ‘outlook’ and other words of similar meaning in connection with a discussion of future operational or financial performance.

This report follows the International Integrated Reporting Framework (www.integratedreporting.org) and should be read in conjunction with the financial statements included herein and the notes thereto. REPORTING FRAMEWORK AND GUIDELINES

This Report details our business model, strategy, significant risks, opportunities and key issues, alongside our overall performance, its resulting outcomes and future prospects for the year. Furthermore, it presents both our financial performance and non-financial aspects, encompassing social, environmental and governance performance The Integrated Report provides information on the business operations (operational and under-construction assets) and sustainability performance of Lodha Developers Limited (formerly known as Macrotech Developers Limited) (herein referred to as ‘Lodha’ or ‘Company’ or ‘we’ or ‘us’ or ‘our’) and its subsidiaries listed in the BRSR, disclosed through six capitals as defined by IIRC. The report primarily focuses on our performance for the reporting period between April 1, 2024 and March 31, 2025. Certain sections of the Report present facts and figures from previous years or information as of the date of approval of the Report to provide a holistic view to the stakeholders.

Beauty and Purpose

Every Lodha development is an invitation to experience rare luxury. We partner with the world’s finest architects and designers to set new benchmarks in luxury living, ensuring that each project enhances not just the skyline but also the lives of those who call it home.

We are guided by a deep appreciation for beauty - in form, in feeling and in function.

Our prestigious developments embody a rare confluence of craftsmanship, aesthetic elegance, unmatched service and elevated experiences. Creating spaces that cultivate kinship, we design homes and communities that foster well-being, celebrate aspirations and enrich lives in ways both tangible and profound; offering our patrons the gift of connection to themselves, to each other and to the world around them.

Lodha stands at the forefront of India’s premium real estate landscape, redefining urban living through thoughtfully designed residential and commercial developments. More than just spaces, our creations are meticulously crafted, nurturing environments that enrich lives through exemplary design, impeccable attention to detail and unparalleled service.

BUILDING A LIFE THAT’S BEAUTIFUL

The essence of luxury living lies not just in where you reside, but in how life unfolds within.

Design Every space tells a story, blending bold architectural statements with purity of form and material. Crisp geometric lines meet neutral interiors, accented with colours and set against lush landscapes in shades of green, celebrating the beauty nature offers.

Service The beauty of luxury lies in seamless, five-star service, where warmth and attention to detail come together to create an atmosphere of effortless elegance. Every interaction is designed to delight, elevate and inspire.

Relationships Our relationships are built on trust. With intuitive service, genuine care and a first-time-right attitude, we continue to create a respected community of stakeholders, residents, partners and collaborators and support them in living their most beautiful life.

Following our philosophy of ‘Do Good, Do Well’, we are committed to using our capabilities to support the nation’s growth and progress and creating a positive impact on the environment and society as an integral part of growing our business.

With over four decades of experience, we have mastered the art of delivering scale without compromise, quality without question and innovation without limits. Our landmark residential, retail and office spaces stand as testaments to our unwavering commitment to excellence, earning the trust and admiration of our patrons and reaffirming our legacy, time and again.

Sustainable Foundations:

Governance for Enduring Value

We believe that a high standard of corporate governance is vital for creating and enhancing long-term stakeholder value. Our corporate governance philosophy reflects the ethos of the Company and our continuous commitment to transparency, integrity, fairness, accountability and ethical business practices.

For more details refer the Corporate Governance Report on page 225 of the Integrated Report.

The Board of Directors is entrusted with the fiduciary duty of safeguarding and enhancing shareholder value by providing strategic direction and ensuring alignment with stakeholder expectations. The Board provides strategic oversight and independent judgment on business operations and strategy, ensuring legal compliance, maintaining the integrity of financial reporting and promoting credibility through timely and accurate disclosures. Furthermore, the Board oversees the effectiveness of our governance practices and risk management systems, upholding the highest standards of transparency and accountability.

The Board has constituted committees to focus effectively on particular areas, thereby ensuring expedient resolution of issues and efficient decision-making processes. These committees function in accordance with their defined charters or terms of reference and their recommendations are presented to the Board for approval.

Abhishek Lodha holds a Master’s degree in Industrial and Systems Engineering from Georgia Tech, specialising in Supply Chain and Logistics. With 20 years of experience, he excels in design, sustainability, finance, business development, strategy, risk management, leadership and governance. Previously, he worked as a Business Analyst at McKinsey & Company in Atlanta, USA. He is also on the Board of Lodha Foundation, Lodha Philanthropy Foundation, RMI Energy Solutions India Foundation, Nutan Nirmata Foundation, Sambhavnath Infrabuild and Farms Private Limited, Hightown Constructions Private Limited and Homecraft Developers and Farms Private Limited.

Rajendra Lodha holds a Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering from M.B.M. Engineering College, University of Jodhpur in Jodhpur. He started his career with Lodha and has 32 years of experience in all facets of real estate development.

Our strong execution also translated into a record collection of H145 Bn - resulting in an impressive operating cash flow of H66 Bn that is a new benchmark for our Company. This year, we expanded our locational diversification, with the addition of 10 new projects with a combined Gross Development Value (GDV) of H237 Bn. Notably, we achieved all this while enhancing our dividend payout by 89% to H4.2 Bn and maintaining leverage at 0.20x of equity. DEAR SHAREHOLDERS,

It is with great pleasure and pride that I present to you our annual review for the financial year 2024-25, a milestone filled year for our Company. The global economy continues to traverse through a period of complexity and uncertainty, shaped by geopolitical tensions across multiple geographies, evolving trade dynamics and fluctuating monetary policy expectations. The past year saw much of the democratic world undergo election cycles, often ushering in new leadership and change in approach. Despite these external headwinds, given its large domestic consumption base coupled with low dependence on external trade relative to other large economies, India continues to stand as a beacon of stability. India has demonstrated remarkable economic resilience and momentum on the back of leadership continuity accompanied by growth-oriented policy making. With strong macroeconomic fundamentals, an ascending global perception and a reformist agenda driving governance, India remains one of the most attractive long term investment destinations worldwide. While there are dark clouds circling over the global economic landscape due to trade tensions, there are a few silver linings which make us optimistic. Moderation in commodity prices, particularly of energy prices, augurs well for a large importer like India. Inflationary concerns in most economies have moderated and central banks in all large economies are expected to adopt a more accommodative stance to boost growth. This shift has allowed emerging economies like India to follow suit, bringing down benchmark interest rates and in turn, reducing the cost of capital for the economy. On the domestic front, while the past year saw some growth challenges due to short-term fiscal and monetary tightening,

as well as election-related disruptions, India’s economic trajectory remains strong. Growth while moderated continues to be robust, reaffirming India’s position as the ‘fastest-growing major economy’. Given the early diagnosis and strong macro base for India, there is optimism of a quick turnaround. Recent income tax breaks for middle income households and policy rate reduction by the RBI augurs well for the mid-income housing segment where our Company has a sizeable presence.

A Year of Delivering Consistently I am delighted to share that our Company has continued to deliver consistent, predictable and profitable growth, exceeding expectations across all parameters. We achieved our highest ever pre-sales of H176 Bn, a strong 21% over the previous year. We successfully sold ~9.5 Mn Sq ft and completed 6,793 homes, helping our customers realise their

and a beneficiary of this evolution. As of 2021, real estate contributed 7-8% to India’s GDP, a modest figure compared to other balanced economies where this hovers in the mid-teens in % terms. During this once in India’s lifetime transition, it is expected that real estate will take its rightful share in the economy as per capita incomes continue to rise and demand will continue to far outstrip supply in this decade and the next. Against this backdrop of sustained industry growth, our Company is strategically positioned to continue to grow pre-sales at ~20% CAGR over a long period (with allowance for moderate annual variance basis macro and geo political factors), whilst keeping leverage conservative a unique outlook in an industry known for its gyrations. It is important to stress the predictability of the business model reduces risk substantially. We have consciously built organisational capability to manage a large number of operating projects across our 3 target segments: mid-income, premium and luxury. With expansion of our operations into 3 cities (Mumbai Region, Pune and Bengaluru), we not only get ample growth opportunities following our supermarket model, but also get exposure to most of the important industries in the Indian economy. This unique diversification across locations, product segments and economic sectors, supports the predictability demonstrated in our pre-sales trajectory. Our judicious mix of ROE accretive JDA projects, along with significant amount of PAT enhancing owned land projects, coupled with an emphasis on conservative, profitability focused underwriting at the time of acquisition, allows us the confidence of delivering ~20% ROE (already achieved on pro-forma basis in FY25). Our strategy on entering any new city is to advance in two phases, the pilot phase which focuses on building the brand, validating the supply chain and strengthening local capabilities; followed by the growth phase. Following the strong performance of our pilot projects, FY25 saw us enter the growth phase in Bengaluru. We have since added three new projects, bringing the total to five in the city. These additions will drive substantial pre-sales growth, supporting our ability to sustain 20% annual

growth. Going ahead, we will focus on scaling our presence in MMR, Pune and Bengaluru and will enter a new city in the pilot phase further increasing the base which supports the sustainability of our 20% pre-sales CAGR. While we remain committed to keeping our leverage at a very conservative level where net debt to equity will be below 0.5x and carrying substantial liquidity at all times, we now also aim to have a reasonable annuity income portfolio over time. Our aim is to have H15 Bn annuity income by 2030 (FY31): which will cover almost the entire interest and salary costs of the Company. During the year, we added two new warehousing projects in Chennai and NCR and have acquired or are in the process of acquiring the stake of our JV partners in the Digital Infrastructure Platform. Leasing at various parks is progressing well and we are continually enhancing our high street retail portfolio alongside our residential projects. We look to meaningfully grow in annuity income in the next few years.

A Commitment to Nation-Building At Lodha, our purpose remains steadfast: To enhance India’s economic strength and contribute wholeheartedly to its transformation into a developed nation.

To this end, my family and I have donated ~1/5 th of the Company’s equity (valued at H~200 Bn / US$ ~2.5 Bn at the time of transfer in October 2024) to the Lodha Foundation, acting on our belief that business success must drive societal progress. The Foundation represents the aspirations of 1.5 Bn Indians, ensuring that all of India will be a partner in and benefit from the growth and success of our Company. Guided by our ‘Do Good, Do Well’ philosophy, we recognise that growth is not just a goal but a responsibility. Every step we take is anchored in ensuring a positive impact on society and the environment. With this gift, the Family wishes to encourage the Foundation to commit itself to long-term programmes and partnerships which make a tangible difference towards India becoming a developed nation (per capita income of US$ 15,000+ in 2023 terms, with top quartile performance in global Happiness and Environmental Performance Indices) by 2047. The Foundation is guided by an eminent Board of Advisors including Mr. Aditya Puri (former MD, HDFC Bank) and Mr. Sanjeev Mehta (former CEO, Hindustan Unilever / HUL). The Foundation focuses on four key transformative areas for holistic nation building: 1. Education excellence for India’s most capable minds, 2. Innovation, with focus on fundamental research in STEM, 3. Environment and 4. Indian Culture. FAVOURABLE DEMOGRAPHY RBI POLICY PIVOT AND INCOME TAX CUT TO SUPPORT DEMAND FOR AFFORDABLE AND MID INCOME HOUSING

BRANDED, TIER-I RESIDENTIAL DEVELOPERS A PREFERRED CHOICE AMONGST HOMEBUYERS

India’s rapid urbanisation is driving a substantial increase in demand for quality urban housing. Driven by the pursuit of better employment opportunities and living conditions, a growing number of people are relocating to urban areas. The United Nations predicts that India’s urban population will surpass its rural population by 2050, signaling a sustained and enduring demand for real estate in urban and metropolitan areas.

The housing market has delivered overall stable growth, despite elevated mortgage rates after sharp increase in repo rate by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) in FY23. Higher interest rates significantly reduced demand for entry-level and lower mid-income homes, the segments most affected by increased mortgage rates, with reduced loan eligibility requiring larger upfront payments. Change in policy stance and policy rate cuts by RBI are expected to stimulate demand in these segments. Income tax rate cut by the Central Government will further augment disposable income in the hands of homebuyers and support demand.

Over the past two decades, the perception of a home in a consumer’s mind has evolved from just being a necessity to a high value consumer product. Previous perceptions of a home being merely four walls and a roof caused consumers to overlook differences between good developers and not so good developers. Following a decade marked by project delays, budget overruns and quality issues, consumers are increasingly prioritising

established brands with a proven history of on-time, within budget and high-quality delivery.

Homes are now seen as status and source of lifestyle upgrade. Homebuyers, similar to consumers of other high-value products, seek the assurance of a reputed brand, which is synonymous with trust and reliability and prefer to buy from branded developers. Market share of listed and leading non-listed developers has doubled to 34% in FY24 from 17% in FY17 and will increase further as trend towards consolidation is expected to continue.

The size of Indian urban households has experienced a paradigm shift, with a growing preference for nuclear families over traditional joint families. This shift has resulted in increasing demand for residential properties, particularly in urban areas.

Recent years have witnessed a decisive shift in consumer preference towards established, branded developers. Driven by concerns over the reliability and quality of tier-2, unbranded developers, this trend has led to significant market consolidation. Within this select group of branded developers, we distinguish ourselves by consistently delivering a superior lifestyle experience across all consumer segments. The strength of the brand, coupled with the ongoing consolidation in the industry, is enabling us to expand our presence in a granular manner across the city, akin to a super-market chain and capture 15% to 20% market share in the cities we operate.

In order to strategically diversify our market presence, we employ a phased approach to entering new cities, prioritising a low risk, calibrated expansion. This strategy involves a ‘pilot’ phase, lasting three to four years followed by a ‘growth’ phase. The pilot phase is focused on establishing a local, empowered team and gaining deep insights into consumer behaviour and the operating environment. During this phase, we will launch very few projects and aim to build our brand through project deliveries so that customers can experience what Lodha brand stands for. Upon achieving brand recognition and establishing a robust operational team, we transition to the ‘growth’ phase, scaling up our operations within the city with the goal of capturing ~15% market share. This deliberate, phased approach ensures sustainable and profitable growth at the city level. This calibrated approach helps us create a sustainably growing and profitable business operation at the city level.

Execution capability is going to be an increasingly critical differentiator among branded developers. Our backward-integrated model with in-house construction capability provides us with a significant advantage. Nearly 50% of our 5,414 employees are dedicated to engineering, design and construction, helping us to deliver the world’s finest developments. This in-house expertise enhances operational agility and eliminates margin leakage to third-party contractors, driving robust profitability.

We have a clear and well-defined strategy of acquiring land parcels for project development with a balanced mix of outright land purchases and Joint Development Agreements (JDAs) with land owners. This approach enables us to strike a balance between leveraging the strength of our balance sheet to acquire new land, while also being conservative on debt. Our goal is to deliver quality products to our customers, achieve 20% pre-sales growth and a 20% return on equity and fully utilise our execution strength optimally without spreading ourselves too thin in the process. To achieve this, we use a balanced land acquisition strategy, combining outright purchases and JDAs which allows us to scale efficiently and deliver high-quality developments. In the steady state we aim to drive 40% of our pre-sales through JDA projects which are capital light in nature.

Having seen and experienced the excesses in the real estate sector in the last decade, we maintain a strict Net Debt to Equity ceiling of 0.5X. We intend to keep debt well below this ceiling, to ensure that debt becomes an enabler rather than being primary growth driver. Growth should and will be driven by a self-sustaining business model, with debt capped at the stated levels. Land acquisition will primarily be funded through operating cash generated by the development business and debt will be employed in an opportunistic manner for strategic expansion.

While residential real estate remains our core competency, we are strategically growing our annuity business in a calibrated manner, in order to de-risk our development activities. Our target is that by FY31, the annuity income should cover the interest expense of the development business and the fixed overheads of the Company. Our annuity income is derived from three key segments. First, the High Street retail, which we will continue to develop alongside select residential projects and select offices. Second, our digital infrastructure business, which serves the dual purpose of providing annuity income while also creating economic activity and providing employment. Third, from the facility management business, which already manages ~70,000 housing units. Over time, we intend to grow this business into a much larger business unit. We intend to focus on these three streams to generate annuity income and do not plan to undertake independent large-scale office or retail developments.

We aim to bring diversity in our product portfolio to help us generate consistent growth. We are the only developer with a presence across mid-income, premium and luxury segments with a wide range of price points starting from H 5 Mn to H 3 Bn. Our pre-sales for FY25 were driven by ~40 operating projects across diverse segments, cities and construction life stages. This project diversity, coupled with a strong sales infrastructure, ensures consistent and predictable pre-sales growth. Our presence across the three cities of MMR, Pune and Bengaluru has further provided diversity in consumer profiles. While MMR has given exposure to the consumers employed in BFSI, media and entertainment and corporate front offices, our diversification in Pune and Bengaluru has brought in consumers employed in manufacturing, IT services and startups. This extensive diversification coupled with our focus on sustenance sales ensures consistent pre-sales and shields us from market downturns across housing segments, locations and GDP sub-segments.

Our Dynamic Risk Framework

Effective risk management is a foundational pillar of our corporate governance. By systematically identifying potential obstacles and threats and implementing mitigation strategies, we ensure organisational agility and optimal resource allocation in the face of evolving circumstances.

ENTERPRISE RISK MANAGEMENT FRAMEWORK

RISK MANAGEMENT PROCESS

Committed to strong risk governance, our comprehensive risk management policy provides clear guidelines for managing risks across the organisation. This policy defines our risk appetite, establishes a robust framework with clear objectives and processes, fosters a risk-aware culture and enhances our competitive edge.

Recognising the fast-paced and evolving nature of the business environment, we proactively manage both opportunities and risks through our comprehensive Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) framework. Aligned with industry best practices, this structured approach ensures the systematic identification, assessment, mitigation and ongoing monitoring of risks across all our operations, with clear accountability and oversight mechanisms in place.

We regularly review and update our risk management processes to ensure their sustained relevance and effectiveness in addressing the spectrum of risks we encounter.

Ensuring quality and preventing errors upfront is a shared responsibility across all levels. Each operating department proactively manages risks as part of their routine activities. The Internal Risk Management Committee systematically reviews our operational functions and activities, commercial framework and technology platforms, ensuring a robust “Maker Checker” principle. The Internal Audit function provides independent assurance on the effectiveness of business operations and the risk management and oversight process. Internal Audit conducts regular reviews and its findings are presented to the Audit Committee on a quarterly basis.

PALAVA - A CITY OF REFINED LIVING

At Palava, refined living is not just a privilege, it is a way of life. Drawing inspiration from Singapore’s visionary urban planning, Palava embraces the acclaimed ‘5-10-15 minute principle’. Designed for seamless walkability, the city ensures that all essential experiences, from leisure and recreation to education and retail, are always a short stroll away. This innovative approach fosters a healthier, more active lifestyle while reducing vehicle dependency, creating cleaner air and a more serene, balanced environment for residents. A planned city where every space, amenity and detail is meticulously designed to elevate everyday moments into extraordinary experiences; from thoughtfully curated, climate-conscious residences to world-class recreational facilities, Palava sets a new standard for sophisticated urban living. Over a decade ago, Palava was envisioned as a solution to the urban chaos and liveability challenges prevalent in the island city of Mumbai. Palava demonstrates an economically viable model of high-quality, smart and sustainable urbanisation, enabled by meticulous planning, thoughtful design and exceptional service and governance. This forward-thinking urban model integrates eco-friendly practices at every level; from efficient building orientations to extensive green spaces and reflective materials that reduce heat absorption. The carefully designed city maximises natural ventilation and reduces heat retention. The strategically placed towers enhance airflow while naturally cool shaded courtyards offer respite from the heat. The orientation of the towers helps minimise internal heat gains on one side, while on the other, it aids in additionally shading tree-lined walkways.

Lush with over 32,000 trees of 200 species and a diverse array of shrubs, grasses, creepers and trees, Palava is as beautifully green as it is cool. The impact of Palava’s climate-conscious design is striking. A 2024 study done by the Lodha Net Zero Urban Accelerator highlights that Palava’s maximum land surface temperature is 3°C cooler than nearby Kalyan-Dombivli and 2°C lower than Mumbai.

Palava stands as India’s first integrated greenfield city, serving as a model for sustainable urbanisation. Designed to be a self-sufficient neighbourhood with easy access to retail, health and wellness, education, places of worship, transportation and even commercial spaces; at Palava, luxury goes beyond state-of-the-art facilities. Planned with intent, the city’s key feature is ‘openness’, with Palava offering four times the average open space per person compared to

Mumbai and embracing every member of the family, including four-legged companions. The Pet Park is a sanctuary where pets can roam freely, socialise and indulge in play. Designed with care, this dedicated space ensures that pets remain active and joyful, making Palava a truly inclusive community where every resident - human or otherwise - thrives. Nearby, elegance and comfort define the Senior Citizen Office, a dedicated, thoughtfully designed space for the

seniors at Palava to gather, meet and form meaningful connections. And, for the ease of our residents, we have routed AC buses between Palava and Mumbai, the commercial capital; for convenient and comfortable everyday travel. Palava demonstrates time and again that every experience can be enriched with purpose. It is a city where comfort is not just lived, it is beautifully woven into the fabric of everyday life.

Together, these efforts foster a more sustainable and low-carbon built environment.

Clean Energy Initiatives: Our commitment to clean energy is evident across our operations. This transition has led to a significant reduction in our Scope 1 and 2 emissions, decreasing by approximately 77% from the FY22 baseline as we shifted our electricity requirements to renewable sources.

The proportion of renewable energy in our total electricity consumption has nearly increased five-fold in last three years, underscoring our dedication to supporting India’s 2070 net-zero target.

Embodied Carbon Reduction: We actively reduce embodied carbon through two key strategies; material efficient design, which optimises structures for performance with fewer resources and adoption of low-carbon alternatives including sustainable materials and circularity principles to minimise the overall carbon footprint in construction.

Our focus on efficient design and circular construction processes minimises waste and optimises material use. CLIMATE CHANGE

Climate change is reshaping the risk landscape, with increasing exposure to floods, cyclones, extreme heat and water scarcity—factors that can directly impact well-being, disrupt infrastructure and business continuity. Our approach is grounded in proactive resilience and design. We integrate climate adaptation and mitigation measures across planning and development, combining passive design strategies, energy-efficient systems, nature-based solutions and low carbon materials to reduce emissions and build climate-resilient assets.

6

We integrate forecasted climate data and regional risk insights into project design through internal tools and expert engagement, enabling developments to remain adaptive to changing climate conditions. Our property management teams are trained in emergency response protocols, providing an added layer of preparedness within our overall resilience strategy. Water resilience is a key focus. In addition to infrastructure solutions like rainwater harvesting and permeable surfaces, we support behavioural change through

awareness campaigns that promote efficient and responsible water use. As a leading real estate developer, we view environmental upgradation as core to sustainable urban development. From walkable, low-carbon neighborhoods to decarbonised construction and shared mobility systems, our climate strategy supports enhancing environmental outcomes, resilience and our net zero goals.

Walkability Our developments are designed with wide and shaded pedestrian pathways to ensure a safe and convenient walking experience. These features reduce reliance on vehicles for short distances, promote active living and contribute to lowering emissions at the community level. Our township projects are planned using the ‘5-10-15 principle’—daily needs and schools are placed within a 5-minute walk, recreational spaces within 10 minutes and essential services such as healthcare and offices within a travel distance of 15 minutes, thereby encouraging walkable, self-sustained neighborhoods.

Shared Transportation To support shared and low-carbon commuting, we integrate bicycle-sharing infrastructure in our township projects

and operate feeder buses within developments and up to nearby public transport hubs. These initiatives promote public transportation over private vehicles and encourage a shift toward more sustainable mobility

Electrification We are actively expanding Electric Vehicle (EV) infrastructure across all our developments to accelerate the transition to clean mobility. Through a strategic partnership with Tata Power, operating as a Charge Point Operator (CPO), EV charging stations are being installed within all residential complexes. To date, over 150 EV chargers have been commissioned across our projects, enabling residents an easy transition to EVs. In FY25, these chargers collectively supported approximately 3.5 million kilometres of low-emission travel.

By leveraging satellite data and applying urban cooling strategies, the initiative offers a replicable model for sustainable urban development, which is critical as rising urban heat emerges as a key constraint on economic productivity and public well-being for millions of Indians.

Supported by IIT Delhi, the Accelerator is presently engaged in testing and scaling the use of Limestone Calcined Clay Cement (LC3) in concrete, which has the potential to reduce emissions by up to 40% compared to conventional Portland cement.

Renewable Energy Super-efficient ACs

The Accelerator supports our energy transition by advancing renewable energy integration across all sites and assets. This includes both on-site generation and off site procurement pathways. By combining existing solutions with innovative approaches, the initiative helps embed clean energy across operations and drive long-term decarbonisation. These efforts have enabled us to reach approximately 10 MW in renewable power purchase agreements, with plans to significantly scale this capacity in the coming years.

In collaboration with RMI and CEPT University, the Accelerator facilitated the testing of super-efficient room ACs at Palava City over nine months. The prototypes delivered 60% energy savings and up to 50% lower peak demand compared to standard models. These results highlight a clear path to reducing grid stress, cutting emissions and scaling next-gen cooling through this technological breakthrough.

Precast Foundation for Isolated Footings To enhance speed and consistency in foundation work, precast footings were introduced for isolated foundations. This method ensures uniform quality, reduces dependency on on-site shuttering and minimises delays due to curing or workmanship variability.

Sacrificial Wall Ties and Tie Rods in External Wall Formwork To mitigate water ingress in external walls, sacrificial wall ties and tie rods were integrated into the formwork system. These elements are designed to remain in place post-concreting, thereby reducing potential water seepage points and enhancing long-term durability.

Wind Safety Screens and Lift Shaft Platforms Prioritising worker safety, wind safety screens were installed along building peripheries, while dedicated platforms were set up at lift shaft voids. These measures ensure safe operations at heights and mitigate the risk of fall hazards in open shaft zones.

Precast Mullion Casting for Block Walls A novel approach to blockwork was achieved using precast mullions, allowing for precise alignment, better aesthetics and reduced on-site labour. This also streamlined the process of installing polished door frames and shutter with higher dimensional accuracy.

Modular Door Frame System Using FCB Subframes A modular system was developed using fibre cement board subframes to facilitate the installation of polished wooden door frames and shutters during final finishing. This prevents premature damage, eliminates re-polishing needs and ensures a seamless aesthetic.

Hybrid Formwork System – Corewall Jumpform + Aluminium Formwork For the first time, a hybrid system combining Corewall Jumpform and Aluminium Formwork was utilised to achieve monolithic casting. This integration enabled faster cycle times and superior structural integrity by reducing cold joints and enhancing alignment.

Self-Levelling Screed for Marble Flooring Replacing the traditional cement-sand bedding, a self-leveling ready-mix screed was deployed under marble flooring. This not only improved surface uniformity and bonding but also expedited laying activities while maintaining the desired finish quality.

Thermal Insulation for Terrace Slabs To improve energy efficiency, thermal insulation techniques were implemented on all terrace slabs covering habitable floors. This intervention reduces indoor heat gain, thereby enhancing occupant comfort and reducing HVAC loads.

Digital Integration of OpticVyu Cameras for Construction Site Management In line with our continued focus on technology-driven construction practices, the deployment of digital tools like the OpticVyu camera system was a key highlight this year. Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) Management

Construction sites are inherently hazardous environments and mitigating occupational health and safety impacts is crucial. We mitigate occupational health and safety risks by fostering a safer and more secure working environment.

Driving a robust safety culture within an organisation requires a multifaceted approach that transcends mere compliance. It necessitates fostering an environment where safety is ingrained in every action and decision, from the executive suite to the frontline worker. This involves

Our Environment, Health and Safety (EHS) Committee plays a pivotal role in fostering a safe and healthy workplace. The committee works closely with worker representatives to ensure their involvement in our health and safety initiatives and programmes.

To cultivate a robust safety culture and reinforce desired EHS behaviours, the committee has established a comprehensive reward and recognition system which aims to positively reinforce employees and workers who consistently demonstrate exemplary adherence to EHS policies and procedures.

We ensure the safety and well-being of our employees and workers through a comprehensive OHS Management System, which includes policies, manuals and procedures. We conduct thorough risk assessments to identify potential hazards and develop safe work method statements (SWMS) for high-risk activities.

We hold internationally recognised certifications like ISO-45001 and ISO 14001-2015, which set out global standards for OHS Management System and environmental management systems respectively. ISO -45001 is implemented at all our facilities and projects in India. These certified locations constitute 100% of office footprint and 100% of people footprint operating from these locations.

We are deeply committed to leveraging our capabilities to strengthen India’s economy and accelerate its transformation into a developed nation. This commitment is manifested through both strategic business operations and impactful philanthropic initiatives. Recognising the interconnectedness of progress, we prioritise meaningful engagement with a diverse array of stakeholders, including customers, employees, workers, residents and value chain partners.

The Lodha Foundation - dedicated for social and environmental impact, is empowered by a substantial endowment of approximately US$2.5 billion (as of October 2024). This significant investment underscores our unwavering dedication to fostering long-term, transformative programmes and partnerships that directly contribute to India’s aspiration of achieving developed nation status. The purpose of the Lodha Foundation is to make a tangible difference to the goal of enabling India to become a developed nation by 2047. The Foundation is driven by 3 KPIs: increasing the GDP per capita of India; improving the happiness index of India; and improving India’s natural environment.

Through these focus areas , the Lodha Foundation strives to create a lasting and positive impact, contributing significantly to India’s journey towards a prosperous and equitable future. Complementing our strategic pillars, we maintain robust community development programmes and deliver high-quality education through our schools within our several developments. We are also dedicated to ensuring that our built environments foster thriving and fulfilling lives for residents. The subsequent sections will detail our flagship philanthropic initiatives and community development endeavors, illustrating our commitment to integrated and holistic impact.

EDUCATION: LODHA GENIUS PROGRAMME (LGP)

Click here to know more www.lodhageniusprogramme.com

As India pursues its path towards becoming a developed nation by 2047, nurturing its brightest young minds is extremely pivotal. Despite being home to an estimated 6 million gifted students, access to high-quality gifted education programmes at scale remains a crucial challenge in our country. To bridge this gap, Lodha Foundation’s Lodha Genius Programme (LGP), in partnership with Ashoka University, has pioneered

a commitment towards identifying, nurturing and mentoring exceptionally talented students across Indian schools. This fully funded, four-week residential summer programme for grades 9-12 is followed by a year-long structured learning and personalised mentorship journey. In FY24, 195 students were selected from over 3,000 applicants, gaining access to world-class faculty, interdisciplinary courses and global opportunities. Building on this strong momentum, in FY25, LGP expanded its reach by selecting 300 gifted students from a highly competitive pool of over 7,000 applicants, ensuring that more bright young minds across India have the opportunity to realise their potential. Notably, three students from previous cohorts have already secured undergraduate admissions at world renowned institutions such as Stanford and Oxford, highlighting the programme’s role in creating pathways to global excellence and leadership for India’s future changemakers.

Ridhakshi Ganjoo, a 16-year-old student from the 2024 cohort of the LGP, is currently in Grade 11 at Government Higher Secondary School, Dadsara, located in Jammu and Kashmir. The LGP played a monumental role in shaping her academic aspirations, helping her realise that STEM can be both intellectually stimulating and socially impactful. The programme provided a nurturing ecosystem of mentors and peers, encouraging questions, curiosity and creative thinking. From conducting advanced experiments at Ashoka University, including mechanics and schlieren photography, to learning coding, lab techniques and problem solving strategies, the programme equipped Ridhakshi with valuable academic and life skills.

Ridhakshi’s pursuit of purpose and passion for creating impact

Having grown up in Pulwama, where beauty coexists with the challenges of frequent shutdowns, unreliable internet and educational disruptions, Ridhakshi deeply values the platform that the LGP has provided. It not only amplified her voice but also empowered her to transform her personal struggles into purposeful action. Today, she is committed to spreading awareness about the programme in her community, encouraging more students from conflict-affected regions to apply and benefit from the life-changing opportunities the LGP offers. Through her ongoing projects and outreach, Ridhakshi is creating a butterfly effect that continues to champion for education, creativity and resilience.

Our educational vision centres on fostering the holistic development of our young learners. We are committed to contributing to the community by cultivating strong-minded and principled leaders of tomorrow. Serving over 7,000 students across six institutions, we offer a comprehensive curriculum spanning IGCSE (Cambridge), CISCE (ICSE & ISC), CBSE and SSC boards. Our network, comprising The Lodha World School, The Lodha Oakwood School and The Shri Ram Universal School, extends across Mumbai, Thane and Palava. Each school implements a bespoke holistic pedagogy, complemented by activities and reflective practices designed to instill a robust value system. We are dedicated to nurturing excellence, rootedness and resilience in our students.

Our schools cultivate intellectual curiosity, physical well-being, creativity and social responsibility through rigorous academics, co-curricular engagement and community initiatives. We foster advanced learning through initiatives like Math and Science Circles and encourage participation in national and international competitions. Our students have demonstrated exceptional achievement, earning over 100 gold medals in mathematics and science Olympiads and over 380 accolades in STEM, sports and the arts.

LODHA SCHOOLS

A holistic approach to ensuring world-class education

Driven by a vision to foster national innovation and research, we are committed to cultivating essential skills and inspiring youth from middle school onwards. We believe a fundamental transformation of curriculum, pedagogy and experiential learning at the school level will bridge the gap between theoretical education and practical application. This will empower students to significantly contribute to STEM-based innovation and research in India. To this end, we have launched Math & Science Circles in our schools, revolutionising the teaching of mathematics and sciences to inspire high-potential students nationwide to pursue pure sciences and their STEM applications.

Our students demonstrated exceptional academic achievement in national and international Olympiads and competitive examinations, securing top ranks in Mathematics, Science, Cyber and Social Studies. Notably, they achieved commendable results in the Harvard Undergraduate Science Olympiad and received prestigious awards, including cash prizes, for innovative real-world solutions in the Innoventure & Tech4Change Challenge. Further validating our academic excellence, our schools attained leading positions in the Education World School Rankings 2024-25 across national, state and city levels.

The Lodha Institute of Teacher Education (LITE) team plays a crucial role in enhancing the quality of education by focusing on curriculum development, teacher support and assessment refinement. Their key responsibilities include reviewing and improving the curriculum to align with educational best practices, evaluating unit and lesson plans to optimise engagement and learning outcomes and conducting classroom observations to provide constructive feedback for teaching enhancement. The team also designs and reviews assessments, facilitates OMR-based evaluations and builds a repository of skill-based questions to strengthen the teaching-learning process. Additionally, they assess the content and effectiveness of PonderBooks for Science and Math to ensure conceptual clarity and application. Through these initiatives, the LITE team continuously works towards elevating academic standards and improving student learning outcomes.

Beyond academics, our schools foster creative, analytical and leadership skills through extensive co-curricular programmes. STEM Exhibitions promoted hands-on learning and students excelled in inter-school competitions, including Aura, Mindspark Expo and the G20 Summit, securing top ranks. Our arts programme showcased student talent in music, drama, dance and literary events, with recognition in cultural festivals. Competitions like Runway Rendezvous and Calicraft further highlighted their artistic achievements.

Our procurement framework has evolved into a dynamic, integrated ecosystem, grounded in strong policies, centralised expertise and local market alignment. In FY25, we intensified our focus on operational efficiency, sustainability and digital innovation, all the while aligning with evolving ESG mandates and global best practices. This proactive approach strengthens our competitive edge by optimising resource utilisation and minimising risks. We continuously refine our strategies to ensure that procurement remains a strategic enabler for our business objectives.

Our procurement function is undergoing a significant digital transformation, building upon our SAP backbone to streamline processes and enhance value chain transparency. Key advancements include the widespread adoption of an e-Tendering platform, which has enabled smarter vendor selection, negotiation and auction management, resulting in improved competitive benchmarking and increased vendor participation. Looking ahead, we are implementing real-time order tracking for enhanced vendor governance and transparency, alongside automating invoice management to establish a comprehensive single window procurement solution. These digital advancements are driving greater efficiency, agility and visibility throughout the entire procurement lifecycle.

This year, we enhanced our Strategic Partnership Programme into a more interactive and insight-driven platform to build long-term, mutually beneficial relationships with key suppliers.

OVERVIEW OF OPERATIONS

Gross Development Value (GDV) of H ~237 Bn. Despite significant investment in growth, our balance sheet remains robust with net debt at H 39.9 Bn, 0.2x of equity, well below the target ceiling of 0.5x. The Company did not receive any financial assistance from the government during the year. During the financial year, we launched 10 new locations or new projects at existing locations. Some of the key launches during the year included Lodha Avalon, Lodha Altus, Lodha Golf View, Lodha Hanging Gardens and Lodha Opulis in MMR and Lodha Massimo and Lodha Altero in Pune. Our strategic roadmap is clearly defined to deliver predictable and robust financial performance, targeting ~20% presales growth and a healthy 20% Return on Equity (RoE), while maintaining a prudent net debt to equity ratio well below 0.5x. This ambitious yet achievable vision is underpinned by four key strategic pillars: 1. Granular growth supported by best-in-class talent and execution 2. Super-market approach to locations 3. Two phase low risk new city entry strategy and 4. Gradually building annuity income streams. To ensure robust and sustainable growth, we employ a "super market chain" approach strategically locating non-competing projects every 2-4 kilometers across our core urban markets.. This approach minimizes dependency on a particular project or location and provides steady and predictable growth in these cities, enabling us to target a significant 15-20% market share in the long term. Having entered a 'growth phase' in Bengaluru during FY25, we are now looking to replicate our super-market strategy in the city, commencing FY26 with five strategic locations, including three new project launches. Our ability to expeditiously launch projects after tying up land has made us the ‘partner of choice’ for landowners, ensuring a consistent pipeline of JDA projects. This was a significant driver enabling us to add ~ H 237 Bn in GDV in FY25. We handed over ~6,800 units to our customers. With construction in full swing, we expect significant ramp-up in deliveries in FY26.

We are a leading real estate developer in India with a strong brand presence across luxury, premium and mid-income housing segments. Our diverse portfolio includes nearly 40 operating projects across three of the largest real estate markets in India: Mumbai Metropolitan Region (MMR) (where we are the largest player with ~10% market share), Pune and Bengaluru. While we are primarily focussed on residential real estate development, we are also leveraging our development capability to build select annuity income streams through facilities management, industrial & warehousing (digital infrastructure) and leasing of select retail & office spaces. We have introduced ‘BelleVie’, a ditigal platform that complements our already established facilities management business, by connecting residents with a diverse range of customized marketplace services. Scaling new heights FY25 was yet another record-breaking year for the Company, with numerous indicators strengthening our conviction that the ongoing housing cycle in India is long-term and structural in nature. This shift is fuelled by the movement of the economy from low-income to mid-income, which has enhanced home buying potential for a significantly larger segment of Indian households, where the underlying aspiration has consistently been present due to both cultural and economic factors. Continuing the momentum from the previous fiscal, the Company achieved its best ever pre-sales of H 176.3 Bn (21% YoY) and best ever collections of H 144.9 Bn (29% YoY), becoming the fourth consecutive year of delivering ~20% pre-sales growth. RISK MANAGEMENT

Effective risk management is one of the pillars of our corporate governance framework. We believe that a robust risk management system is essential for achieving our objectives and goals, identifying potential obstacles and threats and mitigating potential losses. By implementing a comprehensive risk management framework, we ensure that we are well-equipped to adapt to changing circumstances and allocate resources effectively. We have adopted a comprehensive risk management policy which outlines our approach to managing risks across the organisation and sets out clear guidelines defining our risk appetite and implementing a robust risk management framework. Our ERM framework provides a structured approach to identifying, assessing, mitigating and monitoring risks across the organisation. It also ensures that there are clear lines of accountability and oversight in place to ensure that risks are being managed effectively. The Company has constituted a Risk Management Committee consisting of members of the Board and key executives of the Company to identify and assess business risks and opportunities. OUR SUSTAINABILITY JOURNEY

The Board continues to maintain a strong focus on Environmental, Social and Governance (‘ESG’) priorities to ensure long-term value creation for all stakeholders through responsible and forward looking business practices. The ESG Committee plays a pivotal role in guiding this journey. The Commitee reviews and approves key ESG risks and opportunities (including climate change), sets ambitious targets and monitors our performance and external ratings in alignment with our business strategy. Our sustainability efforts this year have advanced significantly, reinforcing our leadership in decarbonising the built environment. We remain committed to achieving net-zero across our operations and developments and since March 2024, we have maintained carbon neutrality across Scope 1 and 2 emissions. Our operations continue to transition to clean energy, with renewable electricity PPAs now exceeding 10 MW across developments. Our built environment decarbonisation strategy also includes actively reducing embodied carbon in materials, deploying passive design, improving equipment efficiency, enabling clean energy access and supporting clean mobility infrastructure. We are proud to have one of the largest green-certified portfolios in the country, now exceeding 60 Mn sq ft. of certified and pre certified space. As we grow, we remain committed to standardising KPIs, tracking impact metrics and embedding sustainability at the core of our design and delivery. Our flagship Lodha Net Zero Urban Accelerator continues to act as a catalyst for innovation and collaboration in urban decarbonisation. In partnership with RMI India Foundation, we field-tested next-generation technologies such as high-efficiency air conditioners and launched the UrjaAnk initiative; India’s first of a kind residential energy behaviour experiment to uncover household electricity consumption patterns. These insights are now informing the landscape of national energy efficiency standards and contributing to India’s energy security agenda. Our pioneering efforts to mitigate urban heat, including nature-based cooling solutions demonstrated at Palava City, further exemplify our model for sustainable urbanisation. Through the Lodha Foundation, we will continue to open-source our learnings, publishing rigorous case studies and research to enable replication across India’s fast-urbanising regions. We remain proud of our continued leadership across global sustainability benchmarks. This year, we were again included in the Dow Jones Sustainability Index (DJSI) and the FTSE4Good Index and retained our position as a Global Sector Leader for residential development in the GRESB rankings. In a significant milestone, we were also recognised as the top-performing real estate company in the Urban Benchmark by the prestigious World Benchmarking Alliance.

SALIENT FEATURES OF THE NOMINATION & REMUNERATION POLICY

1. Objectives of the policy

To set out the criteria for identifying persons who are qualified to become Directors and persons who may be appointed in Senior Management and Key Managerial positions, including their remuneration.

2. Criteria for appointment of Directors, KMP and Senior Management Personnel

a. The NRC shall ascertain the integrity, qualification, expertise and experience of the person identified for appointment as Director, KMP or Senior Management and recommend his/her appointment to the Board. b. The candidate should possess impeccable reputation for integrity, deep expertise and insights in sectors / areas relevant to the Company, ability to contribute to the Company’s growth.

3. Additional criteria for proposed directors a. Should be eligible for appointment as a Director on the Board and should not be disqualified in terms of Section 164 and other applicable provisions of the Act and the Listing Regulations. b. Should have attained minimum age of 25 years. c. Should not hold directorship in more than twenty companies (including private and public limited companies) or ten public limited companies incorporated in India of which not more than seven shall be Indian listed companies. d. Should be able to devote sufficient time and efforts in discharge of duties and responsibilities effectively. e. Re-appointment/ extension of term of any Board members shall be on the basis of their performance evaluation.

4. Additional criteria for independent directors a. Should meet the baseline definition and criteria of “independence” as set out in Section 149 of the Act and the Listing Regulations.

b. Should not hold the position of Independent Director in more than seven Indian listed companies and if serving as Whole-time Director in any Indian listed company then in not more than three Indian listed companies. c. Should not hold any Board/ employment position with a competitor. The Board may in waive this requirement at its discretion.

5. Remuneration to Executive Directors a. Remuneration to Executive Directors shall be in accordance with the provisions of the Act and the rules made thereunder. b. Increments may be recommended by the NRC to the Board which should be within the limits approved by the shareholders. c. Executive Directors shall not be entitled to sitting fees for attending meetings of the Board and its committees. d. If in any three financial years during the tenure of the director, the Company has inadequate profits / losses, the Board may on the recommendation of the NRC and subject to approval of the shareholders, pay minimum remuneration to the Director in terms of Schedule V of the Act.

6. Remuneration to Independent Directors a. Independent Directors shall be entitled to a commission as may be approved by the Board in addition to sitting fees for attending Board / committee meetings. The NRC shall recommend to the Board the quantum of commission for each director based on the outcome of the evaluation process, including factors relating to attendance and time spent in the Board and committee meetings, individual contribution at meetings and contributions made by directors other than in meetings. b. The Company may pay a fair and reasonable expenditure, as may have been incurred by the director while performing his role as a director of the company, in addition to sitting fees and commission. c. Independent directors shall not be entitled to any stock options.

d. The remuneration payable shall be inclusive of any remuneration payable for services rendered by such Director in any other capacity unless the services rendered are of a professional nature and the Committee is of the opinion that the Director possesses requisite qualification for the practice of the profession. e. Where in any three financial years during the tenure of a director, the Company has inadequate profits / losses, the Board may on the recommendation of the NRC and subject to approval of the shareholders, pay remuneration to a director in terms of Schedule V of the Act.

7. Remuneration to Key managerial personnel (other than Executive Directors), Senior Management and other employees

a. The remuneration to key managerial personnel and senior management shall be sufficient to attract and retain talented and qualified individuals suitable for a role. b. Senior Management shall be assigned grades according to their qualifications, work experience

and competencies and their role and responsibility in the organisation. Individual remuneration shall be based on various factors such as job profile, skill sets, seniority, experience, performance and other benchmarking parameters. c. Remuneration to key managerial personnel shall be a balance of fixed and a performance linked variable pay component as per the company policies.. The performance linked variable pay shall be linked to individual and business performance. They shall also be entitled to annual increments which shall be reviewed and approved by the NRC annually. Additionally they may be paid / offered other benefits / perquisites, housing grants and ESOPs as per Company policies.

8. Policy implementation

The NRC is responsible for recommending the remuneration policy to the Board. The Board is responsible for approving and overseeing implementation of the remuneration policy.

CONSERVATION OF ENERGY, TECHNOLOGY ABSORPTION, FOREIGN EXCHANGE EARNINGS AND OUTGO

Particulars as required under the provisions of Section 134(3)(m) of the Companies Act, 2013 read with Rule 8 of the Companies (Accounts) Rules, 2014 in respect of conservation of energy, technology absorption, foreign exchange earnings and outgo etc. are furnished below.

A. Conservation of Energy

We focus on passive design and energy efficiency to bring down the overall operational energy needs. As part of our broader sustainability agenda, we also emphasize material efficiency and the use of low-carbon materials, reducing the embodied energy of the purchased goods and materials used in building construction. 1. Steps taken or impact on conservation of energy a. Passive design measures: At the design stage, we utilize advanced simulation software such as DesignBuilder, Ansys and others to perform comprehensive analyses of ventilation, shading and thermal load. These tools help us optimize building orientation, façade design and internal layouts to enhance natural ventilation and daylight penetration while reducing unwanted heat ingress. We implement passive strategies like cross-ventilation, the stack effect and the strategic placement of windows, vents and shading elements to minimize reliance on artificial lighting and air-conditioning systems, thereby improving energy efficiency across our projects. b. Energy-efficient appliances and equipment: We deploy high-efficiency energy equipment including star rated air conditioners, LED lighting, premium efficiency motors, VVVF drive elevators, advanced parking lighting control systems. Additionally, in commercial buildings, High Coefficient of Performance (COP) Chillers, Building Management Systems (BMS) and Chiller Plant Managers (CPM) are installed to optimize HVAC operations and reduce energy consumption. c. Super-efficient air conditioning field testing: We enabled Global Cooling Efficiency Accelerator and CEPT University, in partnership with RMI to conduct a 9-month field testing of super efficient air conditioners at Palava. The study compared advanced AC prototypes—designed with superior humidity control and energy-saving features— with conventional market-available units. These

prototypes, inspired by Global Cooling Prize winning technologies, were tested in apartments with similar characteristics to ensure consistency. The testing environment presented challenging conditions, with temperatures ranging from 16.5°C to 40.8°C and humidity levels between 20.3% and 90%. We enabled this testing to help generate insights that can inform the market and policy in room air conditioners in India. d. UrjaAnk initiative: UrjaAnk is an energy conservation initiative by Lodha Foundation in collaboration with RMI India Foundation. It aims to decode residential energy usage patterns in India, set context-specific performance metrics, enable data-driven policymaking and foster energy efficient behavior through community engagement. By combining localized data with actionable insights, UrjaAnk promotes energy efficiency as a key element of sustainable urban living. e. Material efficiency and use of low-carbon materials: By prioritizing material efficiency and collaborating with our supply chain to adopt lower-carbon alternatives, we reduce the energy embedded in construction materials. For example, the use of recycled steel significantly lowers the energy required in production compared to steel produced through the blast furnace route. Similarly, increasing the use of Supplementary Cementitious Materials (SCMs) such as fly ash and Ground Granulated Blast-furnace Slag (GGBS) in concrete reduces dependence on clinker, one of the most energy-intensive components of cement, thereby cutting both embodied energy and emissions. 2. Steps Taken for utilizing alternate sources of energy a. All electricity consumed at our construction sites and commercial assets is procured exclusively from renewable sources. This includes a combination of onsite generation through third-party renewable developers, direct procurement from electricity distribution companies offering green power tariffs and open access power procurement models. Where green tariff activation is delayed due to procedural reasons, residual grid electricity is offset by purchasing Renewable Energy Certificates. We also signed a 5MWp Power Purchase Agreement to supply renewable energy to two of our commercial projects during this year.

b. We integrate renewable energy features across our developments, including solar water heating systems and rooftop photovoltaic installations. Over 5.5MW of solar power capacity has been commissioned over residential societies to offset common area electricity consumption. Additionally, more than 5 MW of cumulative solar capacity is operational across multiple buildings to power common loads. 3. Capital Investment on energy conservation equipment a. We invested approximately H 50 lakhs in the UrjaAnk initiative for procurement expert consultation services, monitoring devices and associated infrastructure to support data collection and analysis. This is a program under the Lodha Net Zero Urban Accelerator, towards which our expense is in excess of H 300 lakhs. b. We continue to invest in energy-efficient equipment such as BEE 5-star rated air conditioners, VVVF drive elevators, LED lighting, premium efficiency motors and Building Management Systems, among others. These investments amounted to approximately H48.6 crores during FY25.

B. Technology Absorption

1. Efforts made towards technology absorption We have adopted advanced simulation and analytics tools such as DesignBuilder, ANSYS and others for passive design optimization. In field operations, we have

implemented smart meters, temperature and humidity sensors and IoT-based devices to capture granular energy data. Our teams undergo continuous training to absorb emerging technologies in HVAC, lighting and material efficiency. 2. Benefits derived like product improvement, cost reduction, product development or import substitution These efforts have led to measurable improvements in building energy performance, enhanced occupant comfort, reduced operational costs and data-informed product development. Our field testing efforts have further contributed to the validation of market-ready super-efficient technologies suited to Indian climatic conditions. By advancing localized insights, we are also influencing national and state-level dialogues on urban energy efficiency. 3. Imported technology We import software tools used for design and simulation. However, the majority of construction materials and energy-efficient equipment are sourced domestically. While certain equipment components are still imported, we are witnessing a gradual shift toward local manufacturing, in line with national priorities around self-reliance and supply chain resilience.
